items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: we had Willie to come in there a while on clarinet, take George Lewis' place... I said, sure, I play with George.

ctx.x: It was Lawrence Murray's band, was it?

Yeah, it was Lawrence Murray. He couldn't go on to George Lewis' title because it was an organized band. But George, George Rosenthal told him, let's get him a good city. But he know most of the men's coming up there because he was down here. He came down here when we even was working at the paddock. Then we made another group. We come out the paddock, we made another group. When George, one time George Lewis split his band. Some of these men that won't go on the road like, such as Jim Crow and Kid Howard, with…
Well, uh, Bro. Well, uh, Bro.

ctx.x: How come that Joe got back into the band and you left?

Then, yeah, when I came to Los Angeles, that's why George Lewis told us that they was, they put a, give him a two weeks notice, but I'd play, just pay in advance. That's the union laws. Yeah. So, Joe, King Goodall, try to help but, Earl Hines did that. So we left that morning and that's the same morning that happened to Joe Watkins, because he was living at the hangover club with George Lewis while we was in San Francisco. So when we go down to Los Angeles playing down there, he, well a few days after we was in…
